observations: Photo 0: top of an inline 4-cylinder petrol engine with four coil-on-plug ignition coils on an aluminium cam cover, a yellow dipstick handle and a black oil filler cap marked ENGINE OIL.
Photo 0: small cast lettering on the cam cover is present but too blurred to read; no maker logo is readable.
Photo 1: front of the same engine with alternator, belt pulleys and timing cover attached; a small stamped label on the timing cover is too small and blurred to read.
Photos 0 and 1: the engine sits in a cluttered parts shop among other engines and hoses; the aluminium is fairly clean, the lower pulleys and alternator show dust and grime.
Photos 0 and 1: a 'POSTED ON JIJI' and dealer name watermark runs across the engine; no running clip, no engine code, no receipt or warranty shown.

identity.kind: 4-cylinder petrol engine with alternator, make and engine code not readable
read_from: photo 0 four ignition coils on the cam cover

claims.evidence: No Hyundai or Kia logo, part number or engine code is readable in photo 0 or photo 1; the look is consistent but not proof.
Photo 0 shows four ignition coils in a row on one cam cover.
The aluminium looks fairly clean in photos 0 and 1, but a clean outside says nothing about wear; the pulleys and alternator show grime.
Internal work cannot be ruled out from photos; at best bolt and gasket close-ups could hint at it.
No clip of the engine running and no compression readings.
No receipt or warranty card is shown in any photo.

risks.risk: Make and engine code unknown (for Hyundai/Kia a 1.6, 2.0 or 2.4 petrol engine are priced very differently)
risks.proof: Sharp close photo of the engine code stamped on the block and the cast text on the cam cover
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced; the engine code sets the comparables

risks.risk: Engine does not run, has low compression, knocks or burns oil
risks.proof: Clip of the engine running with sound, with the engine code shown in the same clip
risks.if_unproven: as not running, an engine for rebuild

risks.risk: Internal damage such as water in oil or a cracked head
risks.proof: Photo of the dipstick and the underside of the oil filler cap

risks.risk: Accessories missing on the unseen sides (starter, wiring harness, ECU, AC compressor, sensors)
risks.proof: Photos of all four sides and a list of what is included
risks.if_unproven: as a long block with only the parts visible in photos 0 and 1

proof_requests: Sharp close photo of the engine code stamped on the block, and the cast text on the cam cover
Clip of the engine running with sound, engine code in the same clip
Photos of the other sides of the engine and a list of included parts
Dipstick and oil filler cap photo
Photo of the receipt and warranty card if they exist
Handwritten note with today's date on the engine in shot
response.reason: Four coils confirm a 4-cylinder petrol engine, but no maker, engine code or displacement can be read in either photo, and that code is what sets the comparables. A sharp photo of the engine code is needed before even a worst case price can be set.
